question: A warehouse started with 108 items. In the morning, 100 items were shipped out. Then 5 more were removed. The remaining items tripled for the new count. Finally, 29 more items arrived. How many items did the warehouse have at the end?

A project budget started at 128 dollars in the morning. By midday, 118 dollars were spent. Then 67 dollars were added from a new allocation. By afternoon, 54 more dollars arrived. The final amount was quadrupled for the full year's projection. When the amount was measured in half-dollars (two-dollar units), how much was the projection?

A bakery started with 56 items on sale. In the morning, 80 items were added. The new total was multiplied by 6 (representing packaging). By afternoon, 80 more items were received. By evening, 59 items arrived. Finally, 65 more were added. A distractor: a neighboring shop had 95 items. What was the total bakery inventory at closing?

A production line had 124 units in the morning. They multiplied by 8 (due to efficiency gains). Then 72 units were added from another line. By afternoon, 25 more units joined. By evening, 429 units were shipped out. Finally, 15 units were added to the count. How many units remained at end of day?

A charity began with 77 dollars. They received 38 dollars in the morning. By noon, 27 dollars arrived. By afternoon, 21 dollars more came in. By evening, 33 dollars were donated. Then 149 dollars were spent on a project. How much total did they donate in dozens of dollars?

A document had 177 pages in the morning. By midday, 174 pages were edited and removed. The remaining pages were divided equally into thirds. By afternoon, they doubled the count. By evening, 1 page was lost. Finally, 59 pages were recovered. How many pages did the document contain by end of day?

A gardener had 60 plants initially. In the morning, this quadrupled. They then added 12 more plants. By afternoon, the total multiplied by 7. By evening, everything multiplied by 8 (representing growth projections). His colleague had 45 plants (separate count). How many plants was the final projection in twelve-plant units?

A project had 132 tasks initially. In the morning, 18 tasks were added. This total tripled by afternoon. Then 372 tasks were removed for a different phase. By evening, everything doubled. His co-worker had 95 tasks assigned. How many tasks remained at the end?

A workspace started with 125 items in the morning. By noon, 52 items were added. By afternoon, 20 items were removed. By evening, 49 items were taken out. The final count was multiplied by 6 for storage capacity. How many storage units were needed?

A student had 101 dollars initially. In the morning, they earned 40 dollars. By afternoon, they earned 44 dollars more. By evening, 21 dollars arrived. Then 45 dollars were spent. Their final amount was multiplied by 7 and converted to half-dollar coins. How many half-dollar coins did they have?

A small business started with 23 dollars. They doubled their money in the morning. By afternoon, 32 dollars were spent. By evening, 54 dollars in sales arrived. Then 13 dollars was added from a rebate. The final amount quadrupled for annual projections. A distractor: another business had 85 dollars. What was the annual projection?

A runner completed 200 kilometers during training. The distance was divided equally into 5 legs. Each leg tripled in value for time calculation. The time was multiplied by 7 (for effort units). Then by 8 (for intensity). Finally, 45 minutes were added to the total. When converted to hours (unit change from minutes to hours), how long was the total training duration?

A shop had 117 items initially. The inventory multiplied by 8 (for packaging). Then by 5 more (for bulk orders). Then 26 items arrived. Another 63 items came in. Finally, 55 items were added. When measured in 5-unit bundles (unit conversion), how many bundles did the shop have?

A small donation box started with 32 dollars. In the morning, 73 dollars were collected. By noon, 61 dollars were added. By afternoon, 52 dollars arrived. By evening, 206 dollars was distributed to charity. How much (measured in half-dollar units as a unit conversion) remained?

A factory had 76 units at opening. They added 52 units from production. The count multiplied by 9 (for shipment batches). By midday, it multiplied by 6 more. Then 26 units were added. Finally, the total multiplied by 9 and was converted to dozens (unit change). How many dozens were there?

A warehouse had 137 units. In the morning, 50 units were removed. The remaining multiplied by 8. By midday, it doubled. By afternoon, 614 units were lost. By evening, 234 more were gone. Finally, 44 units were recovered. How many units (measured as half units in a double-unit system) remained?

A student had 57 tasks in the morning. During the morning study session, 10 more were added. By noon, 54 tasks were completed. By afternoon, the remaining tripled. By evening, 47 more were assigned. A distractor: another student had 85 tasks. How many tasks were assigned in total (measured in nines for grouping)?

A builder started with 27 items in the morning. By mid-morning, this quadrupled. By noon, it multiplied by 8 more. By afternoon, it multiplied by 6 again. By evening, 30 items were added. The final count was converted to dozens (unit change from single items to groups of 12). How many items were in the final configuration?

A library collection started at 123 books. In the morning, 73 were added. By noon, 22 more arrived. By afternoon, 32 books were removed. By evening, 4 books were recovered. Finally, 93 were sent to storage. A distractor: another library had 110 books. How many books remained in the collection?

A team had 110 players in the morning. By mid-morning, 4 were removed. The team count multiplied by 4. By afternoon, 82 players left temporarily. The remaining was divided in half. By evening, 68 more joined. A partner team had 95 players (separate count). How many total players did the team have (measured in half-size units)?

A bank account had 66 dollars initially. In the morning, 27 dollars were added. By noon, 31 dollars were withdrawn. By afternoon, 11 dollars were recovered. By evening, 66 dollars were deposited. How much was in the account at the end of the day?

A project had 122 tasks. In the morning, 17 tasks were added. By noon, 75 more were added. By afternoon, the workload tripled. By late afternoon, it multiplied by 8. By evening, it multiplied by 5 more. A distractor: a related project had 95 tasks. When converted to hours of work (unit change), how many units total?

A class had 135 students in the morning. They were divided into thirds (35 students per group originally, but calculation uses /3). By late morning, 71 students were added. By noon, 43 students left. By afternoon, 64 more departed. By evening, the remaining multiplied by 8. His friend managed 110 students (separate). A distractor: another school had 85 students. How many students were in the final count?

A project budget was 218 dollars. In the morning, it multiplied by 7. By afternoon, 1474 dollars was spent. Then 69 dollars in refunds arrived. The amount multiplied by 7 again. By evening, 58 dollars was added. A distractor: another budget was 150 dollars. When measured in 7-dollar units (unit conversion), what was the total?

A production order had 84 units. In the morning, this multiplied by 7. Then 14 units were added. By afternoon, 155 units were removed. The remaining quadrupled. By evening, it quadrupled again. How many (measured in 4-unit batches as a double system) were in the final order?
